intro.title: Build request deduplication layer
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a request deduplication layer, a component that prevents duplicate requests from being processed multiple times to improve efficiency and consistency in a Node.js application. You'll learn the core concept of using a cache or map to track ongoing requests, ensuring that identical requests wait for the first one to complete instead of executing again. The main technologies involved are JavaScript's built-in Map object for storing request promises and async/await for handling asynchronous operations. By the end, you'll have a functional deduplication layer that can be integrated into API handlers or data-fetching logic.
intro.usecase: Request deduplication is essential in Node.js backend systems where multiple clients might make identical API calls simultaneously. This pattern prevents redundant database queries or external API requests in scenarios like e-commerce product pages with concurrent user access, financial dashboard data refreshes, or real-time inventory management systems. By implementing a deduplication layer, developers optimize resource usage, reduce latency, and prevent rate-limiting issues when fetching user profiles, stock prices, or cached content. This technique is particularly valuable in microservices architectures where multiple services might request the same data from shared dependencies.
